svg.title: A cyclotron
svg.desc: Two hollow D-shaped plates, the dees, lie side by side with a gap between them. A uniform magnetic field B passes down through both. An alternating voltage across the gap gives an electric field E there, pointing from one dee to the other. Charged particles follow semicircular paths inside the dees, gain energy each time they cross the gap, and so spiral outward in ever larger semicircles until they leave as an external beam. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A cyclotron adds energy at the gap and bends the path inside the dees
E reverses each half-turn; B into page
Nonrelativistic thin-gap model: m = qB = qΔV = 1. Equal intervals are equal half-turns; energy
changes only at the gap. Relativistic loss of synchronism is excluded.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
